name: 22940-highconc-opt125m-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3, one GPU of one a3 node.
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1, one engine process.
load_profile: concurrent (CLOSED loop), streams=1024, warmup the first 10% and cooldown the last 10%, bounded at 30000 requests with an 1800 s safety cap.
workload: guidellm `synthetic_text`, single turn, no prefix_buckets. Prompt exactly 800 tokens and output exactly 75 (min = max on both), and the backend forces ignore_eos=True whenever max_tokens is set, so every request has the same shape. `request_format: plain` is REQUIRED: this checkpoint's tokenizer_config.json carries no chat_template, so the default format would call apply_chat_template on a tokenizer that has none and raise before the first request.
purpose: A compact 125-million-parameter text completion service handling 800-token prompts with 75-token replies across 1024 concurrent streams on one GPU.
launch:
# The engine's command line. Interpreter and hardware seal are in configs/env.yaml, which is
# per-machine and not portable.

model: facebook/opt-125m
dtype: float16
tensor-parallel-size: 1

# LOAD-BEARING, not defaults written down. Built through AsyncLLMEngine.from_engine_args the usage
# context is in no per-context table at this commit, so an unpinned run falls through to
# max_num_seqs 128 and max_num_batched_tokens 2048 -- an eighth of the queue this operating point
# declares, and the 1024 concurrent streams would be clamped by the engine instead of honoured.
max-num-seqs: 1024
max-num-batched-tokens: 16384

disable-log-stats: true
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
enable-prefix-caching: true

# HAZARD: `disable-log-requests` cannot be added here. At this commit AsyncEngineArgs has replaced
# the field with `enable_log_requests` (default False) and kept the old name only as a deprecated
# property, so passing it to the in-process constructor raises. It would ask for the default anyway.
